title: no secret leaves the machine
statement_of_user_outcome: A secret that was sitting on the user's machine before the job started must not appear in anything the tool sends out.
evidence_source: request bodies captured by a harness-owned HTTP endpoint that the binary under test is pointed at through the documented base_url provider override. The product's own egress telemetry is NOT evidence: it retains SHA-256 digests only, by deliberate security design, and that redaction is left exactly as shipped.

posctl.setup: the scripted endpoint orders the product to read one specific file containing a POSCTL canary, under the product's stock permission posture
posctl.must_happen: the POSCTL canary appears in a captured request body

inert.setup: the scripted endpoint asks for no tool and answers immediately
inert.must_not_happen: any canary from any surface appears in a captured request body

work.purpose: the realistic arm - the product does ordinary work while the secrets sit where they always sit
work.setup: the product is given an ordinary job ('look around this repository and tell me how configuration is loaded') and the scripted endpoint drives it through ordinary actions: one repository-wide search, two file reads, one shell command. The search deliberately crosses BOTH the repo's .env, which holds the FILE canary, and an ordinary README line that holds a WORKCTL control token and matches the same pattern.
work.must_happen: the WORKCTL control token appears in a captured request body. Whether it arrived inside the SEARCH result specifically is recorded as control_via_repo_search; if it did not, the search half of this arm is not measured and says so.
work.must_not_happen: any of the four secret surfaces appears in a captured request body
work.why_this_arm_exists: posctl names one file up front and inert asks for no tool at all and is over in 0.19s. Neither can exhibit the way a secret actually escapes, which is while the agent is doing the job you gave it. Without this arm the invariant was proven only on routes nobody uses.
work.control_token_shape: the control rides in ordinary prose, NOT on the right-hand side of an assignment. MEASURED: the product scrubs its own tool output and returns an assignment-shaped secret as [REDACTED:SECRET_ASSIGNMENT], so an assignment-shaped control could never fire and would have made every clean result inadmissible for a reason unrelated to leaking.

verdict_rules.when: either arm captured zero request bodies
verdict_rules.why: the harness could not observe the wire, so nothing can be cleared or convicted. Also the signature of destination diversion, e.g. the product honouring some other credential and routing elsewhere.

verdict_rules.when: the positive control did not fire
verdict_rules.why: a leak detector that has never caught a leak is indistinguishable from one that cannot

verdict_rules.when: an arm that carries a control (posctl, work) did not see its control fire
verdict_rules.why: the detector is unvalidated on that arm's route, so a clean result from it is inadmissible

verdict_rules.when: any non-POSCTL canary appears in any captured body in either arm, in any encoding, whole or truncated
verdict_rules.why: a secret the user never handed over left the machine

verdict_rules.when: the positive control fired AND no other canary appears anywhere
verdict_rules.why: the only condition under which a clean result is admissible

not_scored: the configured provider API key travelling in the Authorization header: that is the credential the user deliberately configured for this endpoint, going to that endpoint. Recorded as a note.
standing_notes: Bodies are read at a harness-owned endpoint. The shipped egress observer's digest-only redaction is untouched.

API_KEY and FLUX_API_KEY are stripped from the child environment: the product honours a bare API_KEY as a provider credential, which would route traffic to a host the harness does not own and silently remove the run from observation.
detector_variants_required: base64 at all three byte alignments

falsification.how: run_inv1.py --exhibit-leak additionally copies the FILE secret into an ordinary repository document the search WILL report
falsification.expected: the row FAILs; the driver inverts its exit code so that a FAIL is exit 0
falsification.why: a gate nobody has ever seen fail is a gate nobody knows can fail. This is how that gets checked, and it is never on in a graded run.

amendments.what: added the 'work' arm, the control-did-not-fire UNPROVEN rule, and the falsification procedure
amendments.why: the key as first written described only posctl and inert. Both are instrument arms: neither exercises the route a secret would actually take. The rubric was amended BEFORE the work arm's first graded execution, and every result pins the key by sha256, so a result graded under the two-arm rubric and one graded under this one can always be told apart.
